name: St. Regis Le Morne Resort
positioning: The St. Regis Le Morne Resort, Mauritius: an all-suite, all-butler beach resort with colonial-inspired architecture, set beneath the UNESCO-listed Le Morne mountain
best_for: Travelers who want butler service with every suite
Families wanting a kids club for children aged 4 to 12
Active travelers interested in lagoon water sports and a guided hike on Le Morne Mountain

facts.text: The resort is set against the backdrop of the UNESCO-listed Le Morne mountain.
The resort has colonial-inspired architecture and a seaside manor atmosphere.
The colonial-style suites are inspired by the Astors' summer estates.
All suites have a terrace or balcony overlooking the lagoon or the tropical gardens.
All suites come with a standalone bathtub and a walk-in wardrobe.
The Grand Beachfront Villa is set right on Le Morne beach.
Floating Market serves a blend of Thai, Malay, Vietnamese, Indonesian and Singaporean flavors.
Atsuko serves Japanese cuisine with a live teppanyaki station.
The Boathouse Beach Grill's menus emphasize coastal Turkish and Greek dishes made with locally sourced catches.
INDYA brings a modern twist to traditional Indian cuisine.
The Kite Flyers Club is for children aged 4 to 12.
The water sports club offers kayaking, pedal boats, sailing, snorkeling, water skiing, windsurfing and glass-bottom boat trips.

highlights.text: It is an all-suite, all-butler resort.
Sabrage at Sunset is a champagne-opening ceremony held on the beach at golden hour.
Conde Nast Traveler describes it as the first St. Regis in Africa.
L'Ile Mary is the resort's version of the Bloody Mary, a tribute to Mauritian spices and Creole influences.
A guided hike leads to the first plateau of Le Morne Mountain.

considerations.text: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport is approximately 57.4 km from the hotel.
The resort does not provide shuttle service.
Tank tops, swimsuits, cover-ups and athletic wear are not suited for the dining venues.
